name: Demetrius (Demetrius (mentioned in 3 John))
title: A faithful believer with a good testimony
summary: Demetrius is a person mentioned in 3 John who has received a good testimony from everyone, even from the truth itself. The apostle John strongly recommends him to the recipient Gaius, suggesting that Demetrius was a reliable and respected Christian who may have been the bearer of the letter. He stands in contrast to Diotrephes, who opposed John and the church.

keyEvents.title: Good testimony from everyone
keyEvents.description: Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone and from the truth itself. John personally confirms this testimony and encourages Gaius to welcome him.

keyEvents.title: John's personal recommendation
keyEvents.description: The apostle John gives his own testimony about Demetrius and confirms that this testimony is true, showing the high trust John had in him.

keyEvents.title: Contrast with Diotrephes
keyEvents.description: While Diotrephes opposed the authority of the apostles and refused to welcome the brothers, Demetrius was highlighted as an example of the opposite—a faithful and reliable Christian.

keyEvents.title: Encouragement to follow what is good
keyEvents.description: John uses the examples of Diotrephes and Demetrius to encourage Gaius to imitate what is good, not what is evil, and points to Demetrius as a model.

keyEvents.title: Possible bearer of the letter
keyEvents.description: Many Bible scholars believe that Demetrius may have been the one who delivered 3 John to Gaius, which would explain the warm recommendation from the apostle.
